attributes.author: Denet Rasca
attributes.contents: forty-one leaves — levels, boring logs, brine assays, and one folded water-table map of the centre
attributes.if_it_burns: nothing outlives it. No roll entry to fall back on, no duplicate levels, no clerk's abstract eight hundred miles away — only Denet's memory of his own arithmetic, which is not evidence, and which he would have to say out loud in front of witnesses to be worth anything at all.
attributes.opened: chapter 2, at Sixty Wells — once, and only once
attributes.physical: oiled hide, waxed thread, corners worn pale from being carried against a body; under two pounds
attributes.seals: two, both struck and both single-use: the College's lead seal and Denet Rasca's personal seal
attributes.the_catch: there is no fair copy. Denet sealed the packet without entering the finding on the College roll, against the house rule his own seal binds him to, so these forty-one leaves are the whole of the proof. Burning this packet does not destroy the proof in hand while the finding survives elsewhere — it destroys the finding. That is what makes the packet worth buying, and worth burying.
attributes.what_the_statute_cannot_do: the Fourth Article seizes ground and water. It has no reach over paper. The packet is property and stays with whoever is holding it, even on sealed ground.

name: The Sealed Survey Packet
summary: A hide-wrapped bundle the size of a folded coat, stitched shut and sealed twice — once with the College of Levels' lead seal and once with Denet Rasca's own — holding the levels, the boring logs and the water-table map for the plain's centre. It weighs under two pounds and is the heaviest thing in any wagon it rides in. Both seals are single-strike: the packet can be opened exactly once, and after that it cannot be made to look unopened. It is also the only copy of what it says: no fair copy was ever entered on the College roll, so the finding and the packet are the same object.
